title: Gochujang Salmon Bowl
subtitle: Korean glaze, kimchi, brown rice. 5 min prep, 12 min cook.

ingredients.thai_market_tip: Tops Market and Villa carry Norwegian salmon fillets. Ask for the centre cut — even thickness cooks evenly.
Korean aisle at Tops/Villa, red tub. Chung Jung One is the easy default.

ingredients.note: Oil cap — this is your tsp for the day. Don't add a second.

ingredients.thai_market_tip: Tops carries microwave brown rice packs (Mama, S&P, Hosen). 90 sec, done.
Refrigerated aisle. Bibigo (Tops) or any Korean brand. Avoid the sweet ones.

substitutions.note: Pan-grill 4 min per side instead. Lose the omega-3.
Press, cube, glaze and pan-fry tofu. Soft-scramble eggs on top. Still ~48g protein.
Low-carb mode. Frozen cauliflower rice packs at Tops, 90 sec microwave.

steps.text: Whisk gochujang, soy, honey, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and grated garlic in a small bowl. Reserve half the glaze for serving.
Pat salmon dry. Brush flesh side with half the glaze (the other half is for serving).
Heat non-stick pan, medium-high, no oil. Lay salmon skin-down. Press flat 10 sec. Cook 5 min without moving.
Flip. Cook flesh-side 3 min — glaze should caramelise but not burn. Pull when centre is just opaque.
Microwave brown rice packs per label (~90 sec each).
Build bowls: rice base, salmon on top, kimchi + cucumber + spring onion to one side. Drizzle reserved glaze. Sesame seeds over.

serves_with.note: If hitting hard macros: +1 jammy 6-min egg adds 6g protein, 5g fat.

notes: The trick is split-the-glaze: half for cooking (caramelises on the fish), half raw for finishing (keeps the gochujang funk alive). If your gochujang is mild, add a 1/2 tsp gochugaru flakes to the glaze. Skin-on cooking = crispy skin = stop pressing after 10 sec. Don't crowd the pan; do one fillet at a time if your pan is small.
